newsitem.title: JAPAN: Green Cross posts weak earnings due to HIV scandal.
newsitem.headline: Green Cross posts weak earnings due to HIV scandal.

text.p: Japanese pharmaceuticals maker Green Cross Corp reported weak half-year earnings on Friday due to a scandal over HIV-tainted blood products.
The Osaka-based drug maker posted sales of 36.2 billion yen ($320 million) and parent current profits of 520 million yen ($4.60 million) for the first half of the business year.
Current profit is pretax and includes gains or losses on non-operating activities, such as investment in stocks.

The company posted sales of 46 billion yen ($407 million) and parent current profits of 3.2 billion yen ($28.3 million) in the July-December period last year. The company's first half was later changed to April-September.
"Our earnings took a major blow from boycotts of our products," a company official said.

The boycott of its products at medical institutions in Japan followed a scandal in which former Green Cross presidents were arrested in September on suspicion of knowingly selling blood products that could infect patients with the AIDS-causing virus HIV.
"Sales in the first half fell 20 percent from our target due to the scandal. We see sales falling further by four billion yen ($35.3 million) in the second half," the official said.

Green Cross also revised down its full-year earnings forecast. It expects sales to reach 68 billion yen ($601 million), down from a previous forecast of 82 billion yen. It expects a parent current loss of 2.5 billion yen ($22.1 million) from a previously expected profit of three billion yen ($26.5 million). The company also revised down its forecast for group sales in the full year to 112 billion yen ($991 million) from 123 billion yen ($1.08 billion).

It did not supply a figure for group net profit as it is still unsure exactly how much compensation money it will have to pay before the end of March. The drug maker expects to pay a total of about 25 billion yen ($221 million) in compensation to about 2,000 haemophiliacs and other patients who became infected with HIV through the company's blood products.
Faced with the prospect of continued bleak earnings and the huge burden of the compensation payments, the company announced several restructuring measures.
It said it would sell off part of its land holdings and shares in other companies totalling 11 billion yen ($97.3 million) before the end of the 2000/01 business year.

The company also said it would reduce operational costs by a total of 6.3 billion yen ($55.7 million) before the end of March 1998 through such measures as curbing spending in research and development.
It is also considering setting up a subsidiary that would handle the running of its factories. ($1=113 yen)
